source_title: Care of adults with neurofibromatosis type 1: a clinical practice resource of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)
claim_text: IQ may be reduced in adults with NF1 compared with the general population to a similar extent as in children with NF1, and one study of 20 adults with NF1 versus spouse controls found deficits in visual-spatial skills, memory, selective attention and components of executive function.
notes: Full text from locally supplied PDF (Genet Med 2018;20:671-682; not in PMC). Statement made by the ACMG adult NF1 practice resource citing ref 101 Descheemaeker 2013 PMID 23095048; ref 102 Ferner 1996 PMID 8791250. Secondary citation: not independent of the cited primary work; primary paper should be read for strength grading.The 20-adult comparison is a small study.
independence_flags: secondary citation via guideline PMID 30006586 of ref 101, ref 102
